title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of water between the bars.

hints: Water trapped above index i is min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]) - height[i]. You can compute both max arrays in one pass each, or avoid the extra arrays entirely with two pointers tracking a running leftMax/rightMax.

testCases.description: Strictly decreasing then a small rise

optimalSolution.approach: Two pointers from both ends, tracking leftMax and rightMax as running values. Always advance the pointer on the side with the smaller max — that side's trapped water at the current index is fully determined (its own max is the binding constraint, whatever the far side's max eventually turns out to be).

followUpQuestions: Why is it safe to finalize the water above the shorter side without knowing the far side's exact max, only that it's >= the current side's max?
How would you solve this with a monotonic stack instead?
How does this problem differ from Container With Most Water, given both use two pointers on the same kind of input?
interviewerNotes: One of the best 'hard' bars for separating strong candidates — the two-pointer proof (why moving the smaller side is always safe) genuinely trips people up even when they get the code right by memorization. Push on the 'why' if they recite the algorithm too fast.
